metadata.topic: Cell Biology — Similarity Between Bacterial Cell and Plant Cell
metadata.note: 1m: ONE similarity between bacterial cell and plant cell. Key answer: both have a cell wall. Both also have cell membrane and ribosomes — all accepted. Distractors: nucleus (bacteria have nucleoid, not membrane-bound nucleus), chloroplasts (bacteria lack these except cyanobacteria), mitochondria (bacteria lack these).

question.name: CSEC Bio May 2023 Q1b(i) — One Similarity Between Bacterial Cell and Plant Cell
question.text:
Identify ONE similarity between the bacterial cell and a plant cell:

Similarity: [[1]]
question.general_feedback:
Similarities between bacterial and plant cells:

  • Both have a cell wall — (plant: cellulose; bacteria: peptidoglycan) — the classic CSEC answer
  • Both have a cell membrane — controls what enters and leaves
  • Both have ribosomes — for protein synthesis (though bacterial ribosomes are smaller, 70S vs 80S)

Key differences: Bacteria lack a membrane-bound nucleus (they have a nucleoid region), chloroplasts, and mitochondria. These are present in plant cells but absent in bacteria.

groups.label: One similarity between a bacterial cell and a plant cell
groups.diagnostic_hint: Both bacterial and plant cells have a cell wall (though bacterial walls are peptidoglycan and plant walls are cellulose). Both also have a cell membrane and ribosomes. Bacteria lack a nucleus, chloroplasts, and mitochondria — these are NOT similarities.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 6 tokens for 1 slot. 3 correct (any 1 earns the mark). 'Cell wall' is the standard CSEC answer — the most visible similarity from diagram context. 'Cell membrane' and 'ribosomes' are also valid and accepted. 'Nucleus' is wrong — bacteria have a nucleoid (no membrane-bound nucleus). 'Chloroplasts' are absent in bacteria (except cyanobacteria, not tested at CSEC). 'Mitochondria' are absent in bacteria — bacteria carry out respiration across their cell membrane.
